events.title: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif killings
events.summary: On 8 October 1990 clashes broke out on the Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif amid tension over a planned 'Temple Mount Faithful' cornerstone ceremony that the High Court had refused; worshippers threw stones onto the Western Wall plaza and Israeli police fired tear gas, rubber bullets and live ammunition. According to the UN Secretary-General, reports varied between 17 and 21 Palestinians killed and more than 150 wounded by Israeli security forces, while more than 20 Israeli civilians and police were wounded; B'Tselem counted at least 17 Palestinians shot dead on the Mount. The UN Security Council unanimously condemned the Israeli security forces' actions in Resolution 672 and, after Israel refused to receive the Secretary-General's mission, deplored the refusal in Resolution 673. An Israeli government-appointed Commission of Investigation found police lives had been endangered and justified the use of live ammunition, while criticising senior police commanders for failing to prepare despite advance warnings.

events.title: Temple Mount metal-detector crisis
events.summary: On 14 July 2017 three Arab citizens of Israel from Umm al-Fahm shot dead two Israeli Border Police officers, Ha'il Satawi of Maghar and Kamil Shnaan of Hurfeish, at an entrance to the Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif and were killed by police. Israel closed the compound, including for Friday prayers for the first time since 1969, and reopened it on 16 July with metal detectors at some gates; the Muslim Waqf and Palestinian authorities called for a boycott and mass street prayers, and President Abbas suspended official contacts with Israel. OCHA recorded five Palestinians killed and more than 1,000 injured in clashes in and around East Jerusalem in the following two weeks; on 21 July a Palestinian stabbed three members of an Israeli family to death in the Halamish settlement. Israel removed the metal detectors on 24 July, after which OCHA reported tensions fell significantly.

events.title: Sheikh Jarrah evictions and al-Aqsa clashes
events.title_he: שייח' ג'ראח והעימותים בהר הבית, מאי 2021
events.summary: Tension in Jerusalem rose during Ramadan 2021 over Israeli police restrictions at the Old City, a far-right march chanting 'death to Arabs', and court-ordered evictions of Palestinian families from Sheikh Jarrah in favour of Jewish settler claimants; Al Jazeera reported 58 people, including 17 children, faced eviction. Jewish claimants say they lost the land in the 1948 war; the Palestinian families are 1948 refugees resettled there by Jordan and UNRWA in 1956, and Israeli law lets Jews reclaim pre-1948 property with no equivalent for Palestinians. On 10 May Israeli police entered the al-Aqsa compound firing stun grenades and tear gas while Palestinians threw stones; the Guardian reported more than 500 Palestinians and 21 police officers injured, and a seven-month-old Israeli was hurt by stones thrown at a car. The court ruling was delayed and the Jerusalem Day flag march rerouted, but Hamas fired rockets at Jerusalem after its ultimatum expired that evening and Israel struck Gaza, opening the May 2021 Gaza war.

events.title: Huwara shooting and settler rampage
events.summary: On 26 February 2023 a Palestinian gunman shot dead two Israeli brothers from Har Bracha, Hillel Yaniv (22) and Yagel Yaniv (20), as they drove on Road 60 through Huwara south of Nablus. That night hundreds of settlers (a local Palestinian official estimated about 400) attacked Huwara and nearby villages: OCHA recorded at least 37 inhabited houses damaged, 55 private cars and 1,200 scrapped vehicles burned and eight households displaced. Sameh Aqtash, 37, was shot dead in Za'tara; OCHA says the fire came from either settlers or Israeli forces and his brother said soldiers fired; the Palestinian health ministry reported more than 100 injured, most from tear gas. The IDF's regional commander called it a 'pogrom'; Prime Minister Netanyahu urged people not to take the law into their own hands, while Finance Minister Smotrich said on 1 March that Huwara 'needs to be wiped out'.

events.title: Israeli air and ground operation in Jenin camp
events.summary: On 3-4 July 2023 Israel carried out a large air and ground operation in Jenin refugee camp, opening with drone strikes followed by ground troops and exchanges of fire, and withdrew overnight on 4-5 July. The Palestinian Ministry of Health reported 12 Palestinians killed in Jenin, including four children, and 143 injured; one more Palestinian was killed at a protest in Ramallah, and one Israeli soldier was killed according to Israeli officials. OCHA called it the deadliest single West Bank operation since it began recording in 2005, and said more than 3,500 people were displaced during the fighting and the camp's water network was cut.

events.summary: Violence in the West Bank continued alongside the Gaza war from 7 October 2023. The UN human rights office (OHCHR) verified 1,061 Palestinians, including 231 children, killed by Israeli security forces and/or settlers in the West Bank and East Jerusalem between 7 October 2023 and 3 March 2026; OCHA's breakdown to October 2025 attributes the great majority to Israeli forces, about half in Jenin and Tulkarm governorates. OCHA recorded 41 Israelis, including 22 members of Israeli forces, killed by Palestinians in the West Bank and 17 Israelis killed in Israel by West Bank Palestinians between 7 October 2023 and 6 October 2025. In 2025 alone OCHA counted 240 Palestinians and 17 Israelis killed in the West Bank, and more than 10,000 Palestinians were displaced by demolitions, settler attacks and access restrictions by October 2025.

events.summary: OCHA documented more than 1,800 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage in about 280 West Bank communities in 2025, an average of five a day and the highest since it began recording in 2006. events.title: Final approval of the E1 settlement plan
events.summary: In August 2025 the Israeli government gave final approval to the E1 settlement plan east of Jerusalem; Finance Minister Smotrich said it would 'bury the idea of a Palestinian state', and at a September 2025 ceremony Prime Minister Netanyahu declared 'There will be no Palestinian state'. The UN human rights office called the approval an unlawful step to consolidate annexation, saying E1 would cut the links between East Jerusalem, Ramallah and Bethlehem and between the northern and southern West Bank. Tenders for 3,401 housing units were published in December 2025, and a first tender for 1,234 units opened on 18 August 2026, while Israeli groups and Bedouin residents challenged the plan in court. OCHA lists 18 Bedouin and herding communities affected by E1 and at risk of forcible transfer.

events.title: Houthi Red Sea campaign and Galaxy Leader hijacking
events.title_he: מערכת החות'ים בים האדום וחטיפת 'גלקסי לידר'
events.summary: After the outbreak of the Gaza war, Yemen's Houthis began firing missiles and drones at Israel and, on 19 November 2023, seized the cargo ship Galaxy Leader and its 25 crew near Hodeidah, claiming it was Israeli; Israel said neither ship nor crew were Israeli. The Houthis went on to attack shipping they called Israel-linked, killing at least nine mariners and sinking four ships, and diverting much Red Sea traffic around Africa; US and Israeli strikes on Yemen killed dozens of people. Shipping at Eilat fell by 85% by December 2023, half the port staff were suspended in March 2024, and the port suspended operations in July 2025 under debts. The Houthis claimed no attacks after the Gaza ceasefire of 10 October 2025, while threatening to resume if fighting in Gaza resumed.

events.summary: On 21 December 2024 a Houthi ballistic missile struck Jaffa in southern Tel Aviv after interception attempts failed; Magen David Adom reported at least 16 people lightly injured by glass and others hurt on the way to shelters. On 26 December Israel struck Sanaa International Airport, power stations and the ports of Hodeidah, Salif and Ras Kanatib; Houthi media reported three killed and 11 wounded. WHO Director-General Tedros said he and UN colleagues were about to board a plane at Sanaa airport during the strikes and a crew member was injured. An earlier Israeli strike on Sanaa and Hodeidah the previous week had killed nine people, according to Al Jazeera.

events.title: Houthi prime minister killed in Israeli strike on Sanaa
events.title_he: ראש ממשלת החות'ים נהרג בתקיפה בצנעא
events.summary: On 28 August 2025 an Israeli airstrike on a meeting of Houthi officials in Sanaa killed the Houthi government's prime minister, Ahmed al-Rahawi, and several ministers; he was the most senior Houthi official killed in the Israeli-US campaign. The strike followed Israeli strikes on Sanaa on 24 August that health officials said killed 10 people and wounded more than 90, after a Houthi missile that the IDF described as carrying cluster munitions. The Houthis vowed revenge; in September Israeli strikes on Sanaa and al-Jawf killed more than 40 people, including journalists and children, and a Houthi drone wounded 22 people in Eilat.
